title: AI Alignment and Social Choice: Fundamental Limitations and Policy Implications

bias_targets.methodology: Theoretical modeling using social choice theory (Sen's Impossibility Theorem) to evaluate how Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) inherently struggles to democratically aggregate conflicting political preferences (e.g., classifying a political party as fascist).

Theoretical discussion to illustrate the mathematical impossibility of achieving universal AI alignment regarding private individual preferences, such as differing user thresholds for avoiding racial stereotypes and racist speech.

Evaluated theoretically as an example of a specific alignment domain where universal agreement on avoiding gender stereotypes cannot be guaranteed for all users simultaneously due to RLHF preference aggregation limits.
Discussed theoretically as a dimension of alignment that cannot be universally generalized across diverse populations without explicitly narrowing the RLHF training focus.
